setup.accept: I understand that my data stays on this instance, which only I run, and that Zankup has no central service.

setup.next.strava: Strava history and themes come next.

setup.error.code: That setup code is not right. Copy it again from the server logs.

setup.error.accept: Accept how your data is handled to continue.

profile.passkeysHelp: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or screen lock: no password or code.

profile.importSoon: Importing your Strava history and exporting everything arrive in later phases.

reset.title: Choose a new password

reset.noToken: This link is incomplete: ask for a new one.

stats.fitnessNote: Fitness is your 42-day average effort, fatigue your 7-day one, and form the difference: positive means rested.
stats.summaryNote: The figures of the period against the same period a year before. Training load adds up every activity's TRIMP: the longer and the higher your heart rate between your resting and maximum, the more it counts, so an easy hour counts little and a hard one a lot.
stats.noPrevious: Nothing in the same period last year
stats.estimatesEmpty: Estimates appear once you have efforts long enough: 20 minutes of power, or runs of 3 km or more.
estimate.noHistory: No history yet: it shows once the estimate changes.
stats.progressNote: Cumulative distance through each year; the selected year stands out.

stats.efficiencyNote: Speed per heartbeat on your runs: higher means faster at the same HR.

heatmap.title: Your heatmap

routes.title: Your routes
routes.empty: Routes appear here once you repeat one.

latest.title: Latest activity
activity.deleteConfirm: It is deleted with its photos and leaves your totals, records and form. It cannot be undone, and Garmin will not bring it back.
activity.editNote: The original file is never changed: these edits are kept apart and survive reprocessing and imports.
activity.name: Name
compare.title: How these metrics compare

compare.chart: {metric}: Zankup against Strava, one point per activity
compare.largest: The activities that differ the most
compare.notEnough: Not enough activities with this value yet.
compare.scaleHelp: Strava's effort as points per minute in each heart-rate zone, fitted to your own {count} activities (R² {r2}). Nothing here comes from anyone else's data.
data.title: Your data
data.importNote: FIT, TCX, GPX, a Garmin export or your whole Strava history
data.gearNote: Shoes and bikes, with their mileage
export.title: Export all your data
export.help: A ZIP with every original file, your photos and everything else as JSON. It stays ready for seven days.
export.preparing: Preparing… you can leave this page.
gear.title: Gear
gear.help: Shoes and bikes. New activities of a sport get its default gear; mileage counts every activity plus what it had before.
gear.empty: No gear yet. Importing a Strava export brings yours.
gear.habitualHelp: The one of its kind you use most: highlighted here, and new activities of its sports get it first. Only one per kind (shoes, bike…): marking it unmarks the previous one.
gear.deleteConfirm: Delete this gear? Its activities stay, without gear.
gear.overLimit: Past its limit: time to think about replacing it.
import.title: Import
import.help: Bring your history into Zankup. Activities already here are recognised and not duplicated.
import.strava: Strava: the ZIP from Settings → My account → Download or delete your account. Names, descriptions, gear, photos and weather come too; when Garmin already has an activity, Garmin's file wins.
import.garmin: Garmin Connect: the ZIP of your data export.
import.files: Loose FIT, TCX or GPX files, compressed or not.

privacy.tap: Tap the map to place a zone.
replay.title: Replay

shared.privacy: Parts of the route near private places are hidden.

health.noReadiness: Readiness needs a week of HRV or resting HR, plus last night's sleep or your form.
health.syncSlow: Still bringing it in the background: it will show up as soon as it is done.
health.none: No health data yet. Connect Google Health, use a Garmin that records sleep, or read Health Connect from the Android app.
health.readinessNote: Readiness weighs last night's HRV and resting HR against your last 60 days, the sleep score and your training form (TSB).
health.sourcesLink: Sources and which one to prefer
health.google.connected: Google Health is connected: the first sync is on its way.
health.google.error: Google Health could not be connected. Try again.
health.google.off: Not set up on this server (GOOGLE_HEALTH_ENABLED and a Google OAuth client).
health.google.reconnect: Google stopped sharing the data: connect it again.
health.google.missing: Some permissions were not granted, so part of the data is missing.
health.hc.note: Read from the Android app (You → Settings → Health Connect).

health.deleteConfirm: Delete every sleep and daily figure from {source}? It cannot be undone.
health.priorityNote: When several sources recorded the same thing, Zankup picks one automatically: for sleep the one with stages, for HRV the source of that night's sleep, for resting HR and steps the one worn longest. You can choose instead.
mobile.hc.title: Health Connect
mobile.hc.note: Reads sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, SpO₂, respiration and steps from Health Connect and sends them to your Zankup. Nothing is written to Health Connect.

health.google.note: Sleep with stages, HRV, SpO₂ and more from a Fitbit Air or another Google device.
ai.title: Zankup Coach
ai.help: Zankup Coach summarises each activity, writes a report on Mondays and answers your questions. It runs on a small AI model ({model}) and only ever sees aggregated numbers.
ai.off: Zankup Coach turns on as soon as you save an Anthropic key above.
ai.budgetWarning: Close to this month's budget: Zankup Coach pauses when it is reached.
ai.budgetExceeded: This month's Zankup Coach budget is spent: summaries, reports and chat pause until next month.
summary.title: Summary
summary.pitch: The coach reads this activity and compares it with your earlier ones to tell you in a few lines how it went: the effort, the pace and what stands out.
summary.failed: The summary could not be written. Try again.
coach.title: Zankup Coach
coach.intro: Ask about your training. The coach reads your activities, fitness, records and sleep and answers with your numbers.
coach.suggestion.1: How am I doing for a 10K?
coach.suggestion.2: How was last week compared with the one before?
coach.suggestion.4: Have I set any records lately?
coach.error: The coach could not answer. Try again.
coach.budget: This month's Zankup Coach budget is spent: it is back next month.
coach.disclaimer: The coach can be wrong. It only works from your numbers and is not a doctor.
coach.off: Zankup Coach is off. Turn it on in Settings.
coach.unavailable: Zankup Coach turns on as soon as you save an Anthropic key above.
weekly.title: Coach's weekly report
weekly.failed: The report could not be written.
weekly.none: The first report arrives next Monday.
mcp.title: Connect an AI assistant (MCP)
mcp.help: Claude or any other assistant that speaks MCP can ask Zankup about your training, read-only and with the same limits as the coach: aggregated numbers, never your location. Create a token and give it to the assistant as a bearer token for the server URL.
mcp.name: Token name
mcp.created: Copy it now: it is shown only once.
mcp.revokeConfirm: Revoke this token? The assistant using it loses access.

progress.fitnessIntro: How your fitness changes with your training and rest over time.
progress.fitnessInfo: The average load of your training over the last six weeks: it rises when you train consistently and falls when you rest. Activities with heart rate or power count. It has no maximum and is not meant to compare people.
progress.noFitness: No fitness yet: it comes from your activities with heart rate or power.
progress.noStreak: Do an activity this week to start a streak.
progress.streakInfo: Weeks in a row, Monday to Sunday, with at least one activity. This week counts as soon as you do one.
progress.moreDetail: See your progress in more detail
progress.glance.up: Nice work! You logged {value} {period}, {pct} % more than the period before ({previous}).
progress.glance.down: Rest matters as much as effort. You logged {value} {period}, {pct} % less than the period before ({previous}).
progress.glance.same: You logged {value} {period}, the same as the period before. Consistency!
progress.volumeInfo: The sum of your activities over the chosen period, per day (7D and 1M) or per week, against the same span just before. Year to date (YTD) is compared with last year up to the same date.
progress.glance.compareLabel: in the same span {count, plural, one {a year} other {# years}} ago
progress.effortText.below: Weeks like this can be good for active recovery.
progress.effortText.in: You are in the right zone: an effective way to keep fit without stretching recovery.
progress.effortText.above: A harder week than usual: good for progress if you rest afterwards.
progress.effortText.far: A big jump on the weeks before: watch the fatigue and give yourself time to recover.
progress.effortInfo: The sum of the effort of the week's activities, worked out from your heart rate. The range comes from your three weeks before: below it you recover, within it you maintain, above it you load more than usual.
progress.noEffort: No effort yet: it comes from your activities with heart rate.
progress.predictionsIntro: Your current predictions against those of 30 days ago.
progress.predictionsInfo: Times you could run today at each distance, worked out with Riegel's formula from your best recent running effort (the one with the best VDOT, at least 3 km). They change when you run faster or when that effort gets old.
progress.noPredictions: No predictions yet: they come from your runs of at least 3 km.
progress.noGoals: No goals yet. Add one with the +.
progress.whichPeriod: Which time frame do you prefer?
progress.whichKind: What kind of goal do you want to reach?
progress.kindTaken: You already have goals for the options in grey. Choose another kind of goal or edit one.
progress.whatTarget: Moment of truth: what is your goal?
progress.targetInvalid: Sorry, this value is outside the current limits.
progress.goalSaveError: The goal could not be saved.
progress.deleteGoalConfirm: Delete this goal? It cannot be undone.
progress.goalAllSportsNote: All the activity you log will count towards your goal
health.history.title: History
health.history.note: When each source was connected, Zankup brought its last 30 days. This asks Garmin and Google Health for the last year (in the background: it takes a few minutes) and reads it from Health Connect on this phone.
health.history.noteWeb: When each source was connected, Zankup brought its last 30 days. This asks Garmin and Google Health for the last year, in the background: it takes a few minutes.
health.history.queued: Under way: {sources}. The data will show up in Health as it arrives.
health.history.hc: Health Connect: {nights, plural, one {# night} other {# nights}} and {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} sent.
keys.envNote: It comes from an environment variable on the server. A key saved here is used instead.
keys.garminHelp: Garmin Connect's Personal API key. Zankup tries it before saving it, keeps it encrypted and never shows it again.
keys.anthropicHelp: Zankup Coach uses Anthropic's API for summaries, the weekly report and the chat; the cost goes to your account (console.anthropic.com). It is tried before it is saved, kept encrypted and never shown again.
instance.fromServer: It comes from the server's configuration now; a value set here is used instead.
instance.modelHelp: Haiku is quick and cheap, and enough for summaries and reports. Sonnet and Opus reason better but cost much more.
instance.syncEvery: Look for new activities on Garmin every
instance.alertsHelp: When a sync or a backup fails several times, Zankup writes to you here.
instance.resendHelp: E-mails go out through Resend (resend.com): paste its API key here.
instance.backupHelp: Every day a copy of the database and your files goes to S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2, Backblaze, AWS…).
instance.s3SecretHelp: The storage's secret access key, kept encrypted:
progress.zonesInfo: The time you spend in each heart rate or power zone, with the zones in your settings. The zone with the most time, and how its share changed against the same span just before.
progress.noFtp: Add your FTP in Settings to see your power zones.
progress.zoneUp: Your time in zone {zone} went up {percent} % {since}.
progress.zoneDown: Your time in zone {zone} went down {percent} % {since}.
progress.zoneSince.3m: in the last 3 months against the 3 before
progress.zoneSince.6m: in the last 6 months against the 6 before
progress.zoneSince.ytd: this year against the same span last year
progress.zoneSince.1y: in the last year against the one before
progress.zoneAdvice.easy.up: You are putting recovery and easy aerobic work first.
progress.zoneAdvice.easy.down: If you feel tired, more easy time will help you recover.
progress.zoneAdvice.steady.up: A lot of moderate intensity builds fatigue: try polarising, easier or harder.
progress.zoneAdvice.steady.down: Less moderate intensity leaves room to recover and for polarised training.
progress.zoneAdvice.hard.up: You are doing more at high intensity: look after recovery between sessions.
progress.zoneAdvice.hard.down: You have eased off: a good time to absorb the work done.
progress.skillsInfo: Your best power over twelve durations, from 15 s to 1 h, in three skills: sprint, attack and climb. Each sits on a nine-level scale by watts per kilo, from beginners to the best riders.
progress.skillsNoWeight: With no weight in your profile, levels are worked out for {kg} kg. Add it in You → Profile.
progress.skillsScale: At each duration, the {levels} levels run from what a beginner holds to what the best manage, in watts per kilo.
progress.bestsInfo: Your best in each activity: running times by distance and, on the bike, the best power by duration and the longest ride. Medals mark the top three of all time or of each year.
progress.noRecentBests: No medals in the last month.
progress.noBests: No bests at this measure yet.
assistants.title: AI assistants
assistants.intro: Connect Zankup to an AI assistant to ask it about your training, sleep and form from its own app, with your own subscription. It can only read: it never changes anything nor sees your routes or personal details.
assistants.claude.open: In Claude, open Settings → Connectors and tap "Add custom connector".
assistants.claude.paste: Call it Zankup, paste the address and tap "Add".
assistants.claude.allow: Tap "Connect": Zankup opens; sign in if asked and tap "Allow".
assistants.claude.chat: Open a chat in Claude and ask about your training.
assistants.othersHelp: Any MCP-compatible assistant can use the same address. If it cannot connect by itself, create a personal token in Settings → Zankup Coach and MCP and paste it into its configuration.
assistants.privacy: Connecting an assistant lets it read your Zankup activities, metrics, sleep and estimates, as numbers and without locations. You can disconnect it at any time: revoke its token in Settings → Zankup Coach and MCP, or remove it from the assistant's connectors.
oauth.title: {name} wants to access your Zankup
oauth.what: If you allow it, {name} will be able to, on your behalf:
oauth.reads: Read your activities, metrics, sleep, records and estimates, as numbers.
oauth.never: Nothing else: it cannot change anything nor see locations, routes or personal details.
oauth.revoke: You can take its access away at any time in Settings → Zankup Coach and MCP.
oauth.invalid: This link to connect an assistant is not valid or has expired. Try again from the assistant.
report.failed: The report could not be written.
